scope: Ghostery-only roadmap. Existing WardenOne protections remain enabled according to their own defaults; no opponent-specific work is removed to shape a comparison.

checklist.task: Confirm the current WardenOne commit, version, default settings, enabled protections, and whether G-01 through G-09 already exist in some form.
Preserve the Ghostery reference as **tag `v10.6.7`**; note that later Ghostery releases may differ.
Capture WardenOne's current tests, release gate, browser versions, and feature coverage.
Record the precise measurement environment: browser version, operating system, CPU, RAM, ruleset versions, profile state, and settings.
Record known issues from the review without treating untested hypotheses as confirmed defects.
Establish a short before/after regression list for consent, tracker identity, fingerprinting, website recovery, DNR writes, and upgrades.
Create an issue/checklist entry for each G-phase; link its code changes and passing test results when completed.

phases.title: Tracker identity and attribution
phases.coverage: implemented within the documented catalog scope
phases.existing: Activity and Network Logger show local product, organization and category attribution with source links, explicit unknown identities and separate request outcomes.
phases.gap: Catalog coverage is intentionally partial; automatic metadata feeds and URL-path classification are outside this phase.

checklist.task: Audit existing WardenOne tracker metadata and UI before adding another database.

Choose an explicitly licensed, versioned source of tracker **names, organizations, categories, and matching domains/patterns**. Check attribution, redistribution, update rights, and maintenance costs.
Define a compact local metadata schema: tracker ID, name, organization, category, match evidence, dataset version, and confidence/provenance.
Support exact hostname/subdomain boundaries and, where supported, relevant request-pattern matches; avoid substring matching (`notexample.com` must not match `example.com`).
Distinguish **known tracker**, **blocked unknown request**, and **locally suspected tracker**. A domain match alone must not falsely imply proven malicious intent.
Separate **attribution** from **enforcement**: adding metadata must not silently create a block rule.
Make metadata updates recoverable, size-bounded, and atomic from the UI's perspective; invalidate in-memory caches when data changes.
Expose useful attribution in the existing Activity/site details interface without flooding users with labels.
Known tracker maps to the intended tracker and organization.
Two tracker products belonging to one company remain distinguishable.
Unknown domain is not mislabeled; lookalike and shared-hosting domains stay separate.
Replacing the metadata database changes displayed identities without requiring a browser restart.
Corrupt or stale metadata fails safely and never removes otherwise valid security rules.

phases.title: Adaptive identifier evidence
phases.coverage: implemented as detection only within the documented conservative scope
phases.existing: Browser-verified unfamiliar-value reuse produces a separate suspected-identifier Activity row under Tracker learner, using ephemeral HMAC sketches and conservative sensitive-flow exclusions.
phases.gap: Adaptive identifier enforcement remains unimplemented; current evidence deliberately proves the original value reaches the server intact. A separate temporary explicit-name DNR capability test is not a shipped feature.

checklist.task: First document which tracking parameters WardenOne already removes and where (navigation, copied links, selected requests).
Prototype **detection only** for high-entropy values reused across independent first-party contexts. Prefer bounded, privacy-preserving local sketches to raw browsing histories.
Define minimum evidence and expiration rules so a single random-looking value is never automatically declared a tracker.
Exclude likely signed URLs, OAuth and other login flows, CSRF/session tokens, payments, downloads, application IDs, and other legitimate parameters.
Keep a separate label for **suspected identifier**, distinct from a confirmed known tracker.
Determine exactly which URL transformations **Chromium MV3 DNR** can enforce at request time; do not assume a `webRequest` observation callback can rewrite requests.
Before any enforcement, prove with a network trace that the identifier is removed **before the request leaves the browser**.
Make any future experimental removal opt-in or narrowly allowlisted until false-positive testing justifies broader use.
Familiar parameter cleanup still works.
An unfamiliar repeated identifier can be detected with sufficient evidence.
One-off values and legitimate tokens are not automatically stripped.
Redirects, OAuth, downloads, signed URLs, and API calls do not break.
If a requested transformation is impossible under ordinary MV3 APIs, the feature reports **detection only**, not fake blocking.

phases.enforcementAcceptance: Conditional enforcement items are satisfied by shipping no adaptive-removal feature; original-value receipt and explicit detection-only labeling are verified. Future removal still requires opt-in or narrow allowlisting and new pre-egress evidence.

phases.title: Consent outcomes and GPC
phases.coverage: implemented with documented CMP-format and document-policy limits
phases.existing: Truthful failed/dispatched/unverified/saved-state consent outcomes, guarded known-CMP flows, open-shadow discovery and cancellation on erasure or invalid settings. GPC uses early MAIN registration, reversible descriptors and atomic document/initiator-scoped headers that survive request allowances.
phases.gap: Custom CMPs, unreadable state and closed roots remain conservative; native coverage uses controlled fixtures and named browser builds.

checklist.task: Inspect `consent-reject.js` and correct the **attempted click vs. successful action** distinction: do not report `true` just because `.click()` was invoked or after `.click()` threw.
Model results as `attempted`, `dispatched`, `rejected`, `unverified`, and `failed` (or equivalent), rather than claiming consent was rejected from an event alone.
Implement explicit, testable flows for the most common CMPs encountered by WardenOne users (for example OneTrust, Cookiebot, TrustArc), retaining the generic heuristic fallback.
Verify a saved opt-out using CMP state/cookies or other reliable, noninvasive evidence when available; otherwise say **unverified**.
Preserve sensitive-dialog exclusions and protections around login, payment, account, and security flows.
Review consent-wall restoration when no underlying content is available.
If GPC is enabled, expose `navigator.globalPrivacyControl === true` at the appropriate document-start page-world boundary **as well as** sending `Sec-GPC: 1`.
Keep the JavaScript GPC value, header, site exceptions, and extension pause state consistent.
`element.click()` throwing is a failure, not a reported rejection.
A dispatched click without evidence of saved consent is **unverified**.
Known CMP procedures survive late loading and open shadow DOM where supported.
No false interaction with checkout, password, permissions, or security dialogs.
GPC's JavaScript property and network header agree for enabled, disabled, and exempt sites.
Browser E2E tests validate saved consent where measurable, not just banner disappearance.

phases.title: Fingerprint consistency
phases.existing: Adversarial conversion/brand/audio/reflection regressions and native realm, linkability, GPU and application checks complete. Noise stays opt-in; raw signals and workers remain visible.
phases.gap: No claim of universal indistinguishability or anonymity. Population measurements and matched Ghostery performance remain outside G-04.

checklist.task: Inventory every currently altered surface in `fingerprint-realm.js` and related code (canvas text, WebGL, WebGPU, audio, screen, voices, Client Hints, etc.).
Verify whether window, iframe, `about:blank`, cross-origin frame, and worker values contradict one another. Explicitly record surfaces that MV3 cannot or should not spoof.
Test WebGL vendor/renderer values against exposed capabilities and WebGPU information; don't claim a profile that the remaining API values disprove.
Test wrappers' `toString`, constructors, prototypes, property descriptors, object brands, errors, and timing where practical.
Verify audio noise cannot corrupt meaningful application samples or accumulate unpredictably.
Keep intentional compatibility boundaries: don't automatically add canvas-pixel rewriting, CPU-count spoofing, or blanket WebGPU masking.
Run repeated-visit and across-site linkability checks, not just one fingerprint-hash check.
Test real graphics, audio, gaming, document editing, video, and login scenarios.
No new cross-API contradictions introduced.
Known worker/iframe limitations are documented and tested.
Repeated visits have the intended stability behavior.
Common applications keep working and existing fingerprint regressions pass.
Any claim of improved anonymity is supported by a linkability or uniqueness measurement, not merely changed API values.

phases.title: Matched performance
phases.existing: Five-arm frozen-updated-data serial benchmark, exact presets, distributions, profiler attribution, worker lifecycle and separate public-page observations recorded.
phases.gap: No universal winner or equal-protection claim. Public failures and narrow machine/sample scope remain explicit.

checklist.task: Use the **same browser/version/machine**, clean but comparable profiles, identical site corpus, and warmed filter updates.
Benchmark **no extension**, **WardenOne only**, and **Ghostery only**.
Measure both **recommended default** and **maximum practical protection** configurations; publish exact enabled settings.
Run ordinary article pages, heavy DOM changes, eight-frame pages, 30-frame stress pages, real media, and auth-heavy apps.
Record page task time, long tasks, page-load/interaction timing, extension worker activity, renderer/process memory, idle overhead, and worker wake/restart behavior.
Repeat runs, capture distributions (not only best runs), and exclude run order/cache artifacts.
Identify WardenOne's highest-cost feature initialization paths; optimize only where correctness is preserved.
Rerun identical benchmarks after each meaningful performance change; retain unfavorable outcomes.
Environment and scripts are repeatable.
Both competitors are configured and measured comparably.
No security module is silently disabled to win a benchmark.
Results report medians/spread, relevant exceptions, and measurement uncertainty.

phases.title: Outbound privacy contract
phases.coverage: implemented and verified within documented native and source-inventory scope
phases.existing: Machine-checkable outbound inventory, native optional-provider request-shape checks, local observation, retention, erasure and uninstall/reinstall evidence.
phases.gap: The ordinary-browsing trace is bounded to a disposable synthetic site; dynamic page resource destinations and intentionally retained URL paths are disclosed.

checklist.task: Inventory all outbound destinations initiated by WardenOne itself: list updates, build/version checks, optional reputation services, media APIs, and other documented fetches.
In a disposable profile, monitor outgoing extension-origin network traffic during ordinary browsing with optional services disabled.
Assert that tracker-learner observations, per-site browsing history, and local activity data are not sent to a WardenOne-owned reporting endpoint.
Verify **each optional provider** is called only when enabled and receives only the documented minimum data.
Test URL query/fragment/token redaction before logging and before any allowed external request.
Verify site-data clearing, full deletion/reset, expiration, and extension removal leave no unexpected records accessible to WardenOne.
Keep `PRIVACY.md`, permission descriptions, and actual behavior aligned as new features are added.
Outbound destination inventory is machine-checkable.
Normal browsing generates no developer telemetry.
Optional provider toggles and sensitive-data redaction pass browser-level tests.
Data deletion and retention match disclosures.

phases.title: Guided site recovery
phases.coverage: implemented for mapped recent page actions and bounded single-feature recovery trials
phases.existing: Guided current-site panel, exact-request investigation link, 15-minute scoped trials, automatic expiry, undo and previewed local diagnostic export.
phases.gap: Only mapped page actions yield suggestions; network-only matches require the existing Network Logger. Native fixture results do not establish arbitrary real-site compatibility.

checklist.task: Design a user-facing **"Site not working?"** flow that identifies likely recently triggered protections or rules.
Offer the **narrowest reasonable override first**: one rule, one tracker, or one feature on that site, not an all-protection pause.
Make temporary exceptions expire automatically and clearly show remaining time and affected protections.
Keep malware/phishing/high-trust security decisions protected from low-authority automatic compatibility exceptions.
Record enough local diagnostic context to explain a failure without collecting passwords, page content, or full sensitive URLs.
Support safe undo/revert of a diagnostic exception and restoration of original protection after expiry/restart.
Consider a compact, **user-initiated** issue-report export with a preview of redacted diagnostics (no default screenshot or silent upload).
Test shared hosts, public suffixes, authentication providers, media sites, payments, and browser app pages.
An isolated false positive can be fixed without disabling unrelated protection.
Exception scope is correct for lookalike hosts and tenant-hosted sites.
Expiration, reload, restart, and manual undo restore the original rule state.
Diagnostics are redacted and require an explicit user action to share.

phases.title: Adversarial boundaries and failure
phases.coverage: reviewed message and DNR boundaries with simulated regressions and disposable Chromium profiles
phases.existing: Endpoint inventory, sender/payload fuzzing, signed page-world configuration, atomic DNR batches, quotas, priority and interruption coverage are retained. Hostile regex and scope parsing, native invalid transactions and host-permission changes were added or verified.
phases.gap: The browser evidence uses disposable local fixtures and installed Chromium builds; it does not prove compatibility or permission behavior in every browser or on arbitrary websites.

checklist.task: Keep a complete inventory of `runtime.onMessage`, `onConnect`, page-world bridges, and externally exposed extension pages.
Verify website/content-script messages cannot perform settings changes, broad allowlisting, data reads, or privileged network operations.
Regression-test authenticated page-world configuration against forgery, replay, mutated payloads, and worker restarts.
Test hostile custom filter inputs: consecutive unsupported regexes, malformed filters, quota exhaustion, ID collisions, and invalid DNR conditions.
Assert **atomic replacement**: a rejected candidate leaves the previous valid rules installed.
Test simultaneous updates by unrelated rule owners; one invalid owner must not erase successful owners or bypass rule authority.
Verify automatic compatibility rules cannot outrank high-priority security blocks without an explicitly trusted user decision.
Test service-worker interruption between preparing changes, storage acknowledgement, DNR commit, and recovery.
Check permission changes and removal/revocation paths against actual browser behavior.
Invalid input never causes an empty security-rule band.
All privileged message routes enforce appropriate sender and payload validation.
Ownership and security-priority tests hold under failure and restart.
Browser E2E tests supplement, rather than replace, simulated unit tests.

phases.title: Saved-profile upgrades and maintainability
phases.coverage: tested in pinned unpacked Edge profile lanes, with published-asset provenance and documented Store and browser limits
phases.existing: Archive provenance and ownership contracts exist. Existing build-update tests do not establish a real older-release-to-candidate upgrade in the same profile.
phases.gap: Oldest-supported and latest-to-next upgrades preserve decisions, DNR, schemas and cleanup across GitHub/Store profiles; measured small extractions only.

checklist.task: Build an E2E upgrade harness that installs a **real older WardenOne release**, seeds realistic local user state, and then upgrades to a candidate build in the **same browser profile**.
Seed custom filters, site overrides, tracker learner approvals, firewall decisions, consent/GPC settings, and bounded history (excluding real personal data).
Verify settings, protection state, DNR ownership, schema migrations, scheduled cleanups, and stored user decisions survive the upgrade.
Test worker startup/recovery after upgrade, interrupted migrations, failed writes, and revoked permissions.
Check both the normal GitHub build and the Store build profile where their included features differ.
Document which prior release versions are supported for direct upgrades; add representative oldest-supported and latest-to-next tests.
Gradually extract small, stable responsibilities from `background.js` behind tested interfaces; avoid a whole-file rewrite.
Keep exact build/provenance gates, source-to-ZIP inventory checks, and permission-change checks.
Review third-party dependencies and external rule-data revisions as part of release preparation.
Old-to-new upgrade works without wiping user decisions or silently disabling protections.
DNR rules and extension state match the newly saved configuration after recovery.
The packaged release bytes match the reviewed source and pass existing release gates.
Any modularization is behavior-preserving and benchmarked for startup regression.

finalAcceptance.task: Every adopted change solves an identified problem, with a before/after demonstration.
No new high-frequency alerts or excessive false positives.
No compatibility exception silently overrides a critical protection.
No unnecessary telemetry, central account, or reporting service is introduced.
New source data has verified licensing/provenance.
Chromium MV3 supports every claimed enforcement behavior.
Real-browser tests pass, including saved-state upgrades.
Performance and privacy regressions are measured, not assumed away.
User-facing claims and the protection count are updated **only after** implementation and verification.
